summary:
Sphere X is an interactive astronomy catalogue prototype designed to help users explore objects observed by NASA’s SPHEREx mission and connect them with information from other astronomical surveys.

The project brings together a visual sky interface, target search and an individual object information panel. A browser containing 500 stars provides a starting point for exploring the interface and organising astronomical information. These reference stars are distinct from confirmed SPHEREx observations.

The aim is to make complex astronomy data easier to find, navigate and understand. Future development will connect SPHEREx observations and spectral data with complementary catalogues, allowing users to investigate individual objects through a unified interface.

Sphere X provides a foundation for an accessible catalogue that can grow as additional observations become available, supporting discovery, education and further investigation.
details:
Sphere X — SPHEREx Catalog Almanac is a web application prototype that brings astronomical discovery into an accessible, interactive catalogue. Its purpose is to help users find celestial objects, explore their available information and develop a clearer understanding of observations associated with the SPHEREx mission.

HOW IT WORKS

The interface combines a visual sky viewer, target search and an object details panel. Users can navigate the sky, search for a target and inspect information about an individual object. A dedicated browser containing 500 reference stars provides an initial collection for exploring the catalogue interface. Inclusion in this reference collection does not establish that an object has been observed by SPHEREx.

The prototype also explores how information from complementary astronomical catalogues, including 2MASS, can support object discovery. The longer-term aim is to connect individual objects with SPHEREx observations, spectral measurements and supporting information from other surveys, while retaining clear source attribution.

TOOLS AND DEVELOPMENT

The project has been developed using Python, Flask, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with JSON used to organise catalogue entries. Development has taken place in Visual Studio. Work has also included investigating astronomical catalogue services and the handling of SPHEREx FITS data.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Astronomical information is often distributed across specialist services and file formats. Sphere X aims to make the first steps of exploration easier by bringing search, visual navigation and object information into one interface.

The intended audience includes students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts and users seeking an accessible starting point for further investigation. Source information and measurement context are essential so users can understand what each entry represents.

CREATIVE APPROACH

The project approaches the catalogue as an expandable almanac: an individual object becomes a starting point for exploring related observations and information. The design supports both users who know a target’s name and those who prefer to discover objects visually.

CURRENT STATUS AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

The current submission is a working interface prototype with an initial reference-star collection. Further development will focus on reliable ingestion of SPHEREx data, linking observations to catalogue objects, displaying spectra and improving data provenance.

Additional ambitions include support for transient and moving objects, reviewed user contributions and tools for comparing stellar characteristics. These are proposed extensions and are not presented as completed capabilities.

Key design considerations include usability, catalogue identification, coordinate consistency, data quality and a clear distinction between reference data, confirmed observations and future analytical features.
